questions.q: Which people, both men and women, did Yahweh say must be sent away from the camp?
questions.a: Yahweh said to send away everyone who has a skin disease, everyone who has a bodily discharge, and everyone who is unclean because of touching a dead body.

questions.q: What did the Israelites do after Yahweh told Moses to send these people away?
questions.a: The Israelites sent those people outside the camp, just as Yahweh had spoken to Moses.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about a man or a woman who sins against another person?
questions.a: He says that the person is unfaithful against Yahweh and is guilty.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses that a man or woman who sins against another person must do?
questions.a: That person must confess the sin, pay back the full cost of the guilt to the one who was wronged, and add one fifth more.

questions.q: What must the guilty person do with the payment if the wronged person has no close relative to receive it?
questions.a: The guilty person must give the payment to Yahweh by giving it to the priest, along with a ram for atonement. The priest then owns it.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say a man’s wife might do?
questions.a: She might turn aside and be unfaithful to her husband.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say might be true of the wife even though her husband does not know about it?
questions.a: She might have lain with another man and become unclean, but there is no witness against her, and she has not been caught.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say might come over the husband?
questions.a: A spirit of jealousy might come over him, and he would be jealous of his wife, whether she is unclean or not.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say a man must do with his wife if he is jealous and thinks she has sinned against him?
questions.a: The man must bring his wife to the priest with an offering of about two liters of barley flour. He must not put oil or frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy that causes sin to be remembered.

questions.q: What does the priest do first?
questions.a: The priest places the woman before Yahweh. Then he takes holy water in a clay jar and mixes dust from the floor of the Dwelling into the water.

questions.q: Then what does the priest do?
questions.a: The priest lets the woman’s hair down and puts the grain offering of jealousy in her hands. While the priest holds the bitter water that brings a curse, he makes the woman swear an oath. He tells her that if she has not been unfaithful to her husband, the water will not harm her.

questions.q: What did the priest tell the woman would happen among her people if she was unfaithful to her husband?
questions.a: The priest told her that Yahweh would make her a curse among her people by making her abdomen swell and her thigh waste away.

questions.q: What does the water that brings a curse cause if the woman is guilty?
questions.a: The water causes her abdomen to swell and her thigh to waste away.

questions.q: What does the priest do with the curses that he writes in the book?
questions.a: He wipes the curses off into the bitter water.

questions.q: What must the priest do with the bitter water that has the curses in it?
questions.a: The priest must make the woman drink the bitter water.

questions.q: What does the priest do with the grain offering?
questions.a: The priest takes the grain offering from the woman’s hand, holds it up to Yahweh, and brings it to the altar. He burns a handful of it, the memorial portion, on the altar.

questions.q: What does the priest do with the bitter water after he burns the memorial portion?
questions.a: He makes the woman drink the bitter water.

questions.q: What happens to the woman if she has been unfaithful to her husband?
questions.a: Her abdomen swells, her thigh wastes away, and she becomes a curse among her people.

questions.q: What will happen to the woman if she has not been made unclean?
questions.a: She will be free and will be able to conceive children.

questions.q: What is the law of jealousy?
questions.a: It is the law for a woman who turns away from her husband and becomes unclean. It is also the law for a man who has a spirit of jealousy and is jealous of his wife.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the husband and the wife after the priest does all this law?
questions.a: The husband will be free from guilt, but the woman who has done wrong will bear the consequences of her sin.

commentary.text: The unclean to be removed out of the camp, Restitution to be made for trespasses.

Verses 1–10 The camp was to be cleansed. The purity of the church must be kept as carefully as the peace and order of it. Every polluted Israelite must be separated. The wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable. The greater profession of religion any house or family makes, the more they are obliged to put away iniquity far from them. If a man overreach or defraud his brother in any matter, it is a trespass against the Lord, who strictly charges and commands us to do justly. What is to be done when a man's awakened conscience charges him with guilt of this kind, though done long ago? He must confess his sin, confess it to God, confess it to his neighbour, and take shame to himself; though it go against him to own himself in a lie, yet he must do it. Satisfaction must be made for the offence done to God, as well as for the loss sustained by the neighbour; restitution in that case is not enough without faith and repentance. While that which is wrongly gotten is knowingly kept, the guilt remains on the conscience, and is not done away by sacrifice or offering, prayers or tears; for it is the same act of sin persisted in. This is the doctrine of right reason, and of the word of God. It detects hypocrites, and directs the tender conscience to proper conduct, which, springing from faith in Christ, will make way for inward peace.

This law would make the women of Israel watch against giving cause for suspicion. On the other hand, it would hinder the cruel treatment such suspicions might occasion. It would also hinder the guilty from escaping, and the innocent from coming under just suspicion. When no proof could be brought, the wife was called on to make this solemn appeal to a heart-searching God. No woman, if she were guilty, could say “Amen” to the adjuration, and drink the water after it, unless she disbelieved the truth of God, or defied his justice. The water is called the bitter water, because it caused the curse. Thus sin is called an evil and a bitter thing. Let all that meddle with forbidden pleasures, know that they will be bitterness in the latter end. From the whole learn, 1. Secret sins are known to God, and sometimes are strangely brought to light in this life; and that there is a day coming when God will, by Christ, judge the secrets of men according to the gospel, Ro 2:16. 2 In particular, Whoremongers and adulterers God will surely judge. Though we have not now the waters of jealousy, yet we have God's word, which ought to be as great a terror. Sensual lusts will end in bitterness. 3. God will manifest the innocency of the innocent. The same providence is for good to some, and for hurt to others. And it will answer the purposes which God intends.
